strategy.summary: GET /products filters the in-memory catalogue by a case-insensitive name substring `q`, pages results with `limit` (default 20, capped at MAX_LIMIT = 50) and `offset`, and returns `{ total, items }`; non-whole `limit`/`offset` or `limit` < 1 get 400. Integration tests start the real http server on an OS-chosen port (as the existing test does) and assert on the fixed 120-product catalogue.
outOfScope: GET /products/:id and POST /orders (not part of this ticket)
the search box UI (no UI in this repo)
assumptions: The cap is 50, as the code's MAX_LIMIT says (confirmed by the reviewer in Q1); the README's 'up to 100' is stale and is left unchanged per the reviewer.

Tests run the real app in-process via createApp() on port 0; nothing is faked. The catalogue (src/catalogue.js) is fixed, 120 products, 15 per name, so expected totals are known; orders only change stock, not names.
Results are in id order (README: 'by id'), so pages can be asserted by id.

risks.description: Lenient parsing (e.g. Number('2.5') or '-1') lets bad paging through

acceptanceCriteria.text: `q` matches products whose name contains it, in any case; without `q` every product is listed.
Results are paged with `limit` and `offset`, the response's `total` is the number of matches, and limits above the cap (50) are capped.
A `limit` or `offset` that isn't a whole number, or a `limit` below 1, gets 400.

review.standard: Parametrise repetition (test-vitest: use it.each when only the data varies)
review.summary: TC7 and TC8 loop over invalid values inside one test instead of using it.each, so the first failing value hides the rest.
review.failureScenario: Say a regression makes the server accept limit='abc' and limit='' but still refuse '2.5' and '-3'. The loop at line 82 stops at the first failed expect on 'abc', so the report shows one broken value, not two. The same applies to the offset loop at line 91. With it.each({ limit }) each value would be its own named case.

review.standard: Arrange / Act / Assert, one behaviour per test
review.summary: One test checks two behaviours: limit=0 is refused and limit=1 is accepted.
review.failureScenario: If limit=1 broke (for example it returned no items), the failure would show up under a test whose title also covers the refusal of 0, so the title alone doesn't say which boundary failed. Splitting it into 'refuses a limit of 0' and 'accepts a limit of 1' would fix that.

review.standard: Share test helpers: a helper two specs need goes once in a shared module
review.summary: The beforeAll/afterAll setup that starts the in-process server on port 0 is copied line for line from test/products.test.js instead of moved into a shared test helper.
review.failureScenario: Say the server's startup or shutdown later changes (createApp takes options, or close needs closeAllConnections). One copy gets the fix and the other doesn't, and the two specs drift apart. Moving the setup into something like test/support/server.js and importing it from both specs would avoid that.

questions.question: README says GET /products `limit` goes "up to 100", but the code caps it at 50 (MAX_LIMIT = 50 in src/app.js). Which cap is correct?
questions.assumption: The code's cap (MAX_LIMIT, imported from src/app.js, currently 50) is correct and the README is stale; tests assert against the imported constant and the discrepancy is noted as a follow-up.
questions.answer: The cap is 50, as the code does. The README is out of date; leave it as it is and test against 50.
